lead: Google's plan to cut Search for schools that reject AI becomes a political fight in a day, with Sanders, Mamdani and Lina Khan piling on. Anthropic ships FlashProve to prove which model answered you, and Revolut says self-hosting cut its AI coding bill by about 90%.

sections.title: The debt nobody sees
sections.intro: Off-balance-sheet AI obligations at big tech hit $3.2T, and Super Micro's 298% growth shows the demand side of the same boom.

sections.title: The schools fight
sections.intro: Google's plan to cut Search for schools that reject AI draws fire from Sanders, Mamdani and Khan; Google says schools stay in control, and NYC proposes a K-8 generative-AI ban.

sections.title: The proof problem
sections.intro: Anthropic open-sources FlashProve to let users verify which model answered them.

sections.title: The cost curve
sections.intro: Revolut moves to self-hosted GLM and cuts coding inference cost about 90%, while Traversal raises $120M for SRE agents.

sections.title: The data commons
sections.intro: Two essays on what open models need: a posttraining task commons that does not exist, and torrents as the natural way to ship 510 GB of weights.

sections.title: The workbench
sections.intro: Living with agents: one engineer's $3,000-a-month setup and an open-source fraud platform tuned by coding agents.

sections.title: The reskilling case
sections.intro: IKEA turned 8,500 call agents into design consultants after Billie took the routine half of its inquiries.

sections.title: The talent and the lobby
sections.intro: Claude Code's product lead leaves Anthropic, and The Information describes Nvidia's soft power over its customers.

sections.title: The handmade turn
sections.intro: A manifesto for human-made writing and software against AI-generated everything.

sections.title: The reading shelf
sections.intro: A math primer on generative models and an iPad Mini review roundup.

sections.title: The ballot box vs. the data center
sections.intro: The midterms turn data centers into a campaign issue: Democrats win Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Pennsylvania, Ohio towns vote bans, and AI stocks drop.

sections.title: The chip border
sections.intro: Oracle drops a $7B Tencent chip lease, Chinese firms wait on $70B of Nvidia orders, and the FT counts the grid gap behind it all.

sections.title: The research claim
sections.intro: An amateur says Claude Code and Codex helped find an exoplanet candidate; TESS will test it by Nov 26. Pharma leaders doubt the bigger AI-cures-disease promises.

sections.title: Embodied money
sections.intro: Chinese embodied-AI funding rose fivefold in H1 2026.

sections.title: The godfather's warning
sections.intro: Hinton says AI might not have been worth building and warns of a major incident within two years.

sections.title: The number problem
sections.intro: The UK admits its 400 billion pound AI windfall figure came from a Google-commissioned report; its own estimate is under a third.

sections.title: The security desk
sections.intro: Sentra raises $150M to govern what AI agents can read.
